editorial:
Imagine a loud, beer-loving Australian guy heading to the fancy streets of London to get a bit of culture. That is exactly what happens when Bazza and his wild aunt, Edna Everage, land in England. The vibe is total chaos from the start. You get to see a classic fish-out-of-water story where the main character doesn't care about the rules or the posh way of doing things. He just wants to find a cold drink and hang out with his mates in the Australian neighborhood of Earls Court. It is a loud, proud, and very silly ride that pokes fun at both the Brits and the Aussies.

The acting is over-the-top in the best way possible, especially Edna, who steals every scene she is in. While the pacing feels a bit loose and the jokes are very old-school, it still works if you like slapstick humor. If you enjoy comedies that don't take themselves seriously, you will love this.
endingExplained: After all the wild mishaps in London, Bazza realizes that the fancy high society life just isn't for him. He does not suddenly become a cultured gentleman. Instead, he embraces his true self. The movie wraps up with him staying true to his roots and his friends. He finds out that being yourself is better than pretending to be posh, and he ends the journey still loving his beer and his loud Australian lifestyle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school comedies and loud characters.
